hook_text: 864 apples, boxes of 24. Two big bites and you know how many boxes.
clip_script: A farm in Ceres. 864 apples, packed 24 to a box. How many boxes? Do not count one box at a time. Take a big bite: 30 boxes hold 720 apples. 144 are left. Small bite: 6 boxes hold 144. Nothing left. 30 plus 6: 36 boxes. Check by multiplying back: 36 times 24 is 864. Now 500 learners and buses of 32. 15 buses carry 480. 20 learners left over. 15 remainder 20. The remainder is smaller than 32, so no full bus is left to fill. Big bites, add the bites, multiply back.
visual_style: A pile of apples shrinking in two big scoops into rows of boxes, with the box count adding up beside it.
mood: Satisfying, like packing a box perfectly full.
pacing: Two bites, one add, one check, then the remainder twist.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and work out how many boxes of 24 you need for 960 apples.
